meaning: Samsung says 4C (4E on older models) means water is not entering the washer correctly. It is a fill / water-supply problem, not a drain problem.
causes: Water supply taps not fully open, or hoses kinked behind the washer
Clogged mesh filters in the inlet hoses or inlet valve
Hot and cold hoses swapped or not connected to the matching inlets
Drain hose set too deep in the standpipe, so water siphons out as it fills
Faulty water inlet valve
diy: Open both hot and cold supply valves fully and straighten any kinked hoses behind the washer.
Turn off the water, unscrew the inlet hoses and rinse the small mesh screens at the hose ends and valve inlets.
Confirm the hoses are on the correct hot/cold inlets and the drain hose sits only 6 to 8 inches into the standpipe.
Unplug the washer for one minute, restore power and restart the cycle.
call_pro_when: Water pressure and hoses are fine, the filters are clean, and the washer still will not fill.

meaning: Samsung says 5C (5E or nD on older models) means water is not draining from the washer at the correct speed, or not draining at all.
causes: Clogged drain pump filter (coins, hair, lint, socks)
Kinked, clogged or badly positioned drain hose
Blocked household standpipe or sink drain
Excess suds from too much detergent or non-HE detergent
Failed drain pump
diy: Unplug the washer, open the small access door at the bottom front, drain the leftover water into a tray and clean the pump filter.
Check the drain hose for kinks and make sure it is not pushed more than a few inches into the standpipe.
Run water into the household standpipe or sink to confirm it drains freely.
Use only HE detergent in the recommended amount and run a Rinse+Spin cycle to test.
call_pro_when: The filter and hose are clear but the washer still will not drain, or the pump makes no sound at all.

meaning: Samsung says UE (also shown as Ub or UB) means the load inside the tub is unbalanced. Ur means the washer is retrying on its own by adding water and redistributing the clothes.
causes: Laundry bunched on one side, or a single heavy item like a rug or comforter
Load too large, or too small
Washer not level, or shipping bolts still installed on a new washer
Worn suspension rods or shock absorbers
Faulty vibration / imbalance sensor
diy: Open the door, spread the clothes evenly, close the door and restart the spin.
Wash bulky items with a few extra pieces so the weight spreads around the drum. Do not fill past about two-thirds.
Put a level on top of the washer and adjust the leveling feet until it does not rock.
On a new washer, confirm all shipping bolts on the back were removed.
call_pro_when: A balanced load in a level washer still throws UE on every spin, or the drum bangs or wobbles loudly.

meaning: Samsung says dC (dE or dE1 on some models) means the washer does not detect the door as closed and locked.
causes: Door not fully shut, or clothing caught in the door
Debris or detergent residue on the latch or strike
Damaged or misaligned door latch
Failed door lock assembly
Wiring or control board fault
diy: Open the door, remove any laundry or debris from the latch area and close it firmly until it clicks.
Wipe the latch hook and strike plate clean.
Unplug the washer for a minute, then restart the cycle.
Check that the door is not sagging or sitting off-center against the latch opening.
call_pro_when: The door closes cleanly but the code keeps coming back, or the door lock will not release.

meaning: Samsung says the HE / hE / HC family of codes means the dryer is getting too hot, and almost always the reason is restricted airflow.
causes: Clogged lint screen
Blocked or crushed exhaust duct behind the dryer or in the wall
Low supply voltage on electric dryers
Faulty thermistor or high-limit thermostat
Failed heating element or control board
diy: Clean the lint screen. If it feels coated, wash it with warm water to remove fabric softener film.
Disconnect the vent duct behind the dryer and clean it out along with the exterior vent hood.
Make sure the duct is not kinked or crushed when the dryer is pushed back.
Unplug the dryer for a minute, restart and run a timed dry to see if the code returns.
call_pro_when: The code returns after the lint screen and the full vent path are clean.

meaning: Samsung says LC (LE on some models) means the leak sensor in the base detected moisture where it should not be, even if you cannot see a leak.
causes: Water in the base pan from a hose, seal or door gasket leak
Garbage disposal knockout plug not removed after a new install, causing backflow
Too much detergent or suds reaching the sensor
Dishwasher recently moved, splashing water onto the sensor
Faulty leak sensor
diy: Turn the dishwasher off at the breaker or unplug it. It will keep beeping until the sensor is dry.
Check the water supply and drain hose connections under the sink for drips.
If it was just connected to a new disposal, confirm the disposal's dishwasher knockout plug was removed.
Use less detergent, leave it unplugged for several hours so the base can dry, then restore power.
call_pro_when: The code returns after drying out, or you find water in the base pan, because an internal hose or the sump is probably leaking.

meaning: LG says OE means the washer could not drain the water from the wash cycle.
causes: Clogged drain pump filter
Kinked or clogged drain hose
Blocked standpipe or sink drain
Excess suds from too much detergent
Failed drain pump
diy: Check the drain hose for kinks and confirm it is not pushed too far into the standpipe.
Run a Spin Only cycle and listen. A humming pump usually means a clogged filter.
Unplug the washer, open the lower access panel, drain the small hose into a pan and clean the drain pump filter.
Run a Tub Clean cycle and cut back on detergent.
call_pro_when: The filter and hose are clear and the pump is silent, or the washer still will not drain.

meaning: LG says IE is a water inlet error: the tub did not fill to the right level within the expected time.
causes: Supply faucets not fully open, or a hose kinked
Clogged inlet filter screens
Low water pressure
Frozen hoses in cold weather (garage laundry rooms)
Faulty water inlet valve
diy: Open both hot and cold faucets fully and straighten any kinked hoses.
Turn off the water, remove the inlet hoses and clean the mesh filters with a small brush.
Run the faucet into a bucket to confirm the water flow is strong.
In winter, thaw frozen hoses with warm water before restarting.
call_pro_when: The supply is strong and the filters are clean but the washer still does not fill.

meaning: LG says capital UE means the washer stopped because the load is unbalanced and needs you to fix it. Lowercase uE means the washer is still trying to rebalance on its own by adding water and moving the clothes around.
causes: Laundry piled on one side of the drum, or a single bulky item
Load too large or too small
Washer not level
Worn suspension or shock absorbers
Items that hold water unevenly: pillows, bath mats, waterproof jackets
diy: If you see uE, wait. If it turns into UE, open the door and spread the load evenly.
Fill the drum to about two-thirds and add a few items when washing one bulky piece.
Put a level on the washer and adjust the feet so it does not rock.
Avoid washing waterproof items or a single heavy rug alone.
call_pro_when: A level washer with a balanced load still stops with UE on every spin.

meaning: LG says LE means the motor is overloaded and locked, so the tub could not spin. It usually comes from an overload or something jammed in the drum.
causes: Overloaded drum
Coins, keys or other objects jammed between tub and drum
Motor overheated
Faulty motor hall sensor
Failed motor or control board
diy: Unplug the washer for 5 to 30 minutes so the motor can cool, then restart.
Take some laundry out and try a smaller load.
Check the drum for coins, keys or other objects and remove them.
Run a Spin Only cycle with the drum empty to see if the code returns.
call_pro_when: The code returns on an empty, cooled-down washer, or the drum will not turn freely by hand.

meaning: LG says d80, d90 and d95 (Flow Sense) mean airflow is restricted somewhere between the dryer and the outside. The number is roughly how blocked the vent is: 80, 90 or 95 percent.
causes: Lint-clogged exhaust duct inside the wall
Crushed, kinked or coiled vent hose behind the dryer
Exterior vent flap stuck or clogged with lint
Clogged lint filter
Duct run too long or with too many elbows
diy: Clean the lint filter and wash it in warm water if it has a film on it.
Pull the dryer out and check the duct for crushing, kinks or coils. Replace foil hose with rigid or semi-rigid duct.
Go outside and confirm the vent flap opens fully while the dryer runs on Air Dry. Clear lint from the hood.
Reduce the load size and run the cycle again.
call_pro_when: The code keeps coming back after the visible duct and hood are clean, which usually means the blockage is inside the wall run.

meaning: LG says AE (E1 on some models) means a leak inside the dishwasher has tripped the float switch in the base.
causes: Dishwasher not level, so water pools to one side
Dirty or damaged door gasket
Excess suds from the wrong detergent or too much of it
Clogged spray arms throwing water at the door
Internal hose, sump or pump seal leak
diy: Turn the dishwasher off at the breaker and check it with a level. Adjust the legs.
Clean the door gasket and look for tears.
Remove and rinse the spray arms.
Use only dishwasher detergent filled to the dispenser line, then remove the kickplate, sponge out the base and let it dry 24 to 48 hours before resetting.
call_pro_when: The base fills with water again after drying and leveling, because an internal part is leaking.

meaning: LG says Er FF is a freezer fan error, Er rF is a refrigerator fan error and Er IF is an ice maker fan error. All three usually come from frost or ice building up around the fan until it cannot turn.
causes: Frost buildup jamming the fan blade
Door left ajar, or a worn gasket letting humid Texas air in
Air vents blocked by overpacking
Failed evaporator or ice maker fan motor
Defrost system failure (heater, sensor or control)
diy: Unplug the refrigerator, take the food out and leave the doors open at least 8 hours so it can fully defrost.
Soak up the melt water with towels and dry the inside.
Plug it back in and give it 24 to 48 hours to get back to temperature.
Check that the door gaskets seal, the doors close fully and no food is blocking the vents.
call_pro_when: The code returns after a full manual defrost, or frost keeps forming on the back wall, which means the defrost system has failed and it will keep happening.

meaning: Whirlpool says F21 (F02 on some models) means draining is taking longer than expected. On newer models the same problem shows as F9 E1: the washer cannot drain correctly.
causes: Clogged drain pump filter
Kinked or clogged drain hose
Drain hose pushed too far into the standpipe, or sealed with tape so there is no air gap
Excess suds from non-HE detergent
Failed drain pump
diy: Press Pause/Cancel, unplug the washer for 5 minutes and restart.
Check the drain hose for kinks and make sure it goes no more than about 4.5 inches into the standpipe with an air gap.
Unplug the washer, open the lower front panel, drain into a shallow pan and clean the pump filter.
Clear the small drain holes in the door seal and use only HE detergent.
call_pro_when: The filter and hose are clear and the washer still will not drain, or the pump does not run.

meaning: Whirlpool and Maytag say F5 E2 means the door (or the lid on a top-loader) is not locking properly.
causes: Door not fully latched, or clothing caught in the opening
Overloaded drum pressing against the door
Dirty or misaligned latch
Failed door lock assembly
Wiring or control fault
diy: Open the door, clear any laundry from the opening and close it firmly.
Reduce the load so the clothes tumble freely.
Unplug the washer for 5 minutes to reset, then restart.
Look at the latch hook and strike for debris and wipe them clean.
call_pro_when: The door closes properly but the washer still will not lock, or the lock will not release.

meaning: Whirlpool says F20 (FH on some models) is a water supply problem. On newer models the same thing shows as F8 E1 or LF: the washer is not seeing the right amount of incoming water.
causes: One or both supply faucets closed, or hoses kinked
Clogged inlet valve screens
Low water pressure, or flood-stop hoses that tripped
Drain hose installed so water siphons out during fill
Faulty water inlet valve
diy: Open both hot and cold faucets fully. The washer needs pressure from both.
Turn off the water, remove the hoses and clean the inlet screens with a brush.
Straighten kinked hoses and reset flood-stop hoses if you have them.
Confirm the drain hose goes about 4.5 inches into the standpipe and is not taped, then unplug for 5 minutes and restart.
call_pro_when: Water flows strongly from both faucets and the screens are clean but the washer still will not fill.

meaning: Bosch says E24 means the dishwasher is not draining, usually because the filter is blocked. E25 means the drain pump itself is blocked, or its cover is loose or missing.
causes: Clogged filter or debris in the sump
Blocked or kinked drain hose
Garbage disposal knockout plug never removed
Drain pump cover loose or missing
Failed drain pump
diy: Remove the lower rack, twist out the filter and rinse it clean.
With the filter out, pop off the drain pump cover, remove any glass or debris from the impeller and snap the cover back until it clicks.
Check the drain hose under the sink for kinks. On a new disposal, confirm the knockout plug was removed.
Reset the dishwasher and run a rinse cycle.
call_pro_when: The filter, pump area and hose are clear and the dishwasher still leaves standing water.

meaning: Bosch says E15 means the safety switch found water in the base of the dishwasher and the leak protection system shut it down.
causes: Leak from a hose, the door seal or spray arm overspray
Excess suds from the wrong detergent
Blocked filter causing an overflow
Water splashed into the base during a move or installation
Leaking sump, pump seal or inlet valve
diy: Turn off the water supply and switch the dishwasher off at the breaker.
Look for water under the sink and around the door seal.
Pull the dishwasher forward slightly and tilt it back to let the base pan drain, or leave it unplugged until dry, then restore power and test.
Use only proper dishwasher detergent and clean the filter.
call_pro_when: The code returns after the base has dried, which almost always means an internal leak that will only get worse.

meaning: On Frigidaire and Electrolux dishwashers, i30 means water has collected in the base pan and tripped the leak / flood switch.
causes: Water in the base pan from a door gasket or hose leak
Excess suds from the wrong detergent
Overfilling from a stuck inlet valve
Internal leak at the sump, pump seal or hoses
Faulty float switch
diy: Cancel the cycle, then turn off the water and the power at the breaker.
Look for drips under the sink and along the door gasket.
Use only dishwasher detergent and clean the filter.
Let the base dry for a day, restore power and run a short cycle to test.
call_pro_when: Water comes back to the base pan after drying out, because something inside is leaking.

meaning: GE says F7 usually points to the key panel: a stuck or shorted key. F2 means the oven temperature went above its safety threshold.
causes: Stuck or shorted key on the control panel (F7)
Moisture or grease in the keypad ribbon connection (F7)
Faulty oven temperature sensor (F2)
Sticking oven relay on the control board (F2)
Failed electronic oven control board
diy: Turn the range off at the breaker for 1 to 2 minutes, then restore power and see if the code clears.
Wipe the control panel dry and press each key to find one that sticks.
For F2, do not use the oven until it is checked. The cooktop burners are usually still safe to use.
If the code comes back, leave the range off at the breaker until it is serviced.
call_pro_when: The code returns after a breaker reset, or right away for F2 if the oven overheats or will not shut off.
